shusher.title: SHUSHER
lines: Shushers. Tall, stooped librarians in grey cardigans, with no mouths, just a finger permanently pressed to where a mouth should be, and ears the size of dinner plates, turning, always turning, towards any sound.

The Stacks have one rule: silence. The Shushers enforce it. A footstep too loud, a cough, a page turned too sharply, a fart in the reading room, and they come gliding out of the shelves, dozens of them, going 'SHHHHHHHH' in a sound like a gas leak.
Then they go 'SHHHHHHHH' harder. And harder. Until your eardrums burst, and then everything is very quiet indeed, and the Shushers are very satisfied.
Strengths: they hear everything, they come in numbers and their shush is a weapon. Weaknesses: they're slow, and they can't stand noise. Make enough of it and they'll clutch their heads and flee.
Tiptoe. Seriously. Tiptoe everywhere on this floor. Hold your farts in. Your life depends on it.

bookwyrm.title: BOOKWYRM
bookwyrm.sub: Something that lives in the shelves. And reads.
lines: Bookwyrms. Long, pale, many-legged creatures made of pages, with a spine for a spine and a mouth full of paper-cut teeth, burrowing through the shelves of the Stacks like woodworm the size of a canoe.
They eat books. They've eaten whole sections of the library. Periodicals is mostly gone. The Large Print section is a hollow shell with a very fat bookwyrm sleeping in it.
Everything they've eaten, they remember. Every word. They'll quote you Shakespeare while they're chewing on your leg. Some of them have eaten so much poetry that they hiss in iambic pentameter.
Strengths: they ambush from the shelves, their bite gives you a paper cut you'll feel for a week and they climb anything. Weaknesses: fire. Obviously. They're made of paper.
Kill one and it'll disintegrate into a drift of loose pages. Read them. Sometimes they ate something important.

head_librarian.title: HEAD LIBRARIAN
head_librarian.sub: Boss of the Reading Room. Silence is mandatory.
lines: The Head Librarian. A tall, thin woman with grey hair in a bun so tight it pulls her eyebrows up, half-moon glasses on a chain, a cardigan buttoned to the neck and the absolute, terrible authority of someone who's run a library for four hundred years.

The Reading Room is her domain. She sits at the great desk, stamping books, watching. Nobody speaks. Nobody coughs. Nobody turns a page without her permission. Breaking the silence in her Reading Room is the one crime in the Stacks with a death sentence.
She's not cruel. She just loves silence more than she loves people. And honestly, after four hundred years of people, who can blame her?
Strengths: her shush is a shockwave, she commands every shusher in the Room and her date stamp hits like a hammer. Weaknesses: she can't bring herself to make noise. Make her.
Out-shush her. It's the only way. Stand in the Reading Room and go 'SHHHHHHHH' louder than she can. She'll fall silent. Forever.

overdue.title: OVERDUE
overdue.sub: Boss of the Returns Chute. Your fines are waiting.
lines: Overdue. A great heap of unreturned books given shape and fury, with a library card for a face, a date-stamp for a fist and a voice made of every late-fee letter ever sent, screaming in the dark at the bottom of the Returns Chute.

Everything returned to the Stacks goes down the chute, and everything that goes down the chute comes back wrong. Overdue is where it all ends up: every book late, every fine unpaid, every 'I'll take it back next week' that never happened.
Yes, there's one of yours in there. You know the one. You borrowed it in 2009. The fine is now in the low millions.
Strengths: books thrown like bricks, a crushing weight of guilt that literally slows you down and an avalanche of returns. Weaknesses: return something. Anything.
Settle your fines with Overdue and it shrinks, book by book, until it's just one sad little paperback on the floor, and it says 'thank you', and you feel like shit for 2009.

paper_golem.title: PAPER GOLEM
paper_golem.sub: The Bindery's workers. Folded, not born.
lines: Paper Golems. Seven-foot figures folded from huge sheets of paper, origami men with stitched spines and faces of printed text, rustling as they move, with paper-cut edges on every limb.

The Bindery makes them. Old manuscripts, pulped and pressed and folded into servants. Each one is made from a book, and each one is that book. That one's a cookbook. That one's a romance novel. That one's a tax law, and he's a fucking nightmare.
They work the Bindery in silent rows, binding books, stitching pages, folding more golems out of whatever's lying around. Including, occasionally, contestants.
Strengths: they're tough for paper, they slice and they keep reforming from loose sheets. Weaknesses: fire. Water. Scissors. A strong breeze.
If you hear one rustle behind you, don't turn round. Just set fire to it.

bindery_foreman.title: BINDERY FOREMAN
bindery_foreman.sub: Boss of the Bindery. Binds anything. Anyone.
lines: The Bindery Foreman. A hulking paper golem folded from a book the size of a wardrobe, with a needle and thread like a harpoon and a guillotine for one hand, presiding over the Bindery's presses like a foreman on a factory floor.

He binds things. Books, mostly. But anything can be bound. He's bound contestants between hardback covers, pressed flat, every word they ever said printed on the pages. They're on the shelves in the Stacks. You can take them out. They're overdue.
He's not a monster. He's a craftsman. He takes enormous pride in his work. His stitching is immaculate. His spines never crack.
Strengths: a guillotine chop that'll take your arm off, a binding thread that pins you in place and a summons that wakes every golem in the Bindery. Weaknesses: unbinding. Cut his stitches.
Unbind him and he unfolds, page by page, into a single flat sheet of paper on the floor. It's his life story. It's surprisingly moving.

index_clerk.title: INDEX CLERK
index_clerk.sub: Boss of the Index Vault. Issues passes. Never has.
lines: The Index Clerk. A tiny, wizened man behind a high counter in the Index Vault, surrounded by card catalogues, with an inkpad, a rubber stamp, a pass book and absolutely no intention of letting you through.

He issues passes to the Restricted Section. He has issued no passes since the first season. Not one. Every application is lost, misfiled, incorrectly completed or rejected on a technicality. The form is forty pages long. Page thirty-two asks for a pass.
He serves the Index, the god of memory. Everything is recorded. Nothing is forgotten. Nothing is allowed in that hasn't been properly filed. And you, my friend, have not been properly filed.
Strengths: he files you away mid-fight, his stamp hurts and the whole Vault defends him. Weaknesses: he can't refuse a correctly completed form. Fill it in. All forty pages.
Or knock him off his stool and take the pass. It's quicker. He'll file a complaint. Nobody will read it.

the_archivist.title: THE ARCHIVIST
the_archivist.sub: Floor Boss of the Restricted Section. Keeps the only key.
lines: The Archivist. A tall, robed figure with no face, just a blank page where a face should be, slowly writing itself. Its hands are quills. Its robes are shelves. It has been reading your book for a very long time.

It keeps the Restricted Section, where the Builders' first records are kept. The Archivist has read them all. It knows what the Stack is for. It knows why you were taken. It knows exactly how your story ends, and it's been waiting for your book to reach this chapter.
It's not your enemy. It's the keeper of the truth, and it has decided the truth is too dangerous. Its job is to make sure nobody reads the last page. Including you.
Strengths: it writes your moves before you make them, it summons bookwyrms and shushers and it can erase your buffs with a stroke. Weaknesses: improvise. Do something that isn't in the book.
Get the key. It'll let you have it, in the end, with a sigh. 'Very well,' it'll say. 'Turn the page.'

the_restless.title: THE RESTLESS
lines: The Restless. Grey, shambling dead in the rags of costumes: villagers, monks, maids, peasants with pitchforks, all of them from the cast of Season Nine, the Network's horror season, still playing their parts decades after the audience died.

They were contestants. They were cast as the dead of Castle Dread. They died for real during filming, and the castle simply kept them on. They walk the graveyard, moan at the windows and leap out of coffins on cue, every night, exactly on schedule.
They're not trying to kill you. They're trying to scare you. Killing you is just how the scene ends.
Strengths: they grab, they swarm and there's always another one coming out of the ground. Weaknesses: they're actors. Break the script and they don't know their next line.
Clap when one scares you. Go on. Give them a round of applause. Some of them will stop and bow. It's the first applause they've heard in forty years.

gravedigger.title: GRAVEDIGGER
gravedigger.sub: Boss of the Graveyard. Always room for one more.
lines: The Gravedigger. A hunched, enormous man in a filthy coat and a stovepipe hat, with a lantern in one hand and a shovel the size of a canoe paddle in the other, digging, always digging, at the edge of the castle graveyard.

He digs the graves for Castle Dread. He's dug thousands. Every contestant who dies on Floor 14 gets a headstone in his graveyard, with their name and their season, and he tends them every night by lantern light, muttering their names.
There's always a fresh grave open. There's always one, waiting. He likes to be prepared. He'll measure you with his eyes while he's talking to you. He's already got your size.
Strengths: his shovel hits like a car, he pulls the Restless up from the earth and he fights in the dark. Weaknesses: his lantern. Smash it and he can't see.
Read the headstones before you leave. You'll find names you know from the shrine on Floor 1.

waxwork.title: WAXWORK
lines: Waxworks. Perfect, glossy, lifelike wax figures of people, standing in poses: mid-step, mid-scream, mid-sentence. They're beautiful. They're detailed down to the eyelashes. And they move when you're not looking.

The Wax Witch made them. She makes them out of people. Dip a contestant in wax, let it set and you have a statue that's still alive inside, still aware, still trying to scream with a mouth that won't open.
When she commands them, they walk. Stiffly. Creaking. Leaving drips of hot wax on the floor behind them. They don't want to hurt you. They don't get a vote.
Strengths: they're hard as candles, they hit like statues and they don't feel a thing. Weaknesses: heat. Melt them.
If you melt one, there's a person inside. Mostly. Sometimes. Be ready for that.

wax_witch.title: WAX WITCH
wax_witch.sub: Boss of the Witch's Tower. Keeps a key in a candle.
lines: The Wax Witch. A tall, pale woman made half of wax, dripping constantly, with candles burning in her hair and a face that slides slowly down her skull and has to be pushed back up every few minutes.

She lives in the tower on the crag above Castle Dread, with her collection of waxworks around her. She was the Season Nine witch. The castle cast her, and she took the part far too seriously and never, ever stopped.
The castle's second key is inside a candle on her altar. She's never lit it. She's afraid of what she'll lose if she does.
Strengths: hot wax that sets on your skin, waxworks that rise to defend her and fire she controls. Weaknesses: her own heat. She's made of wax. She melts.
Melt her and she'll puddle onto the floor of her tower with a sound like a sigh. The candle on the altar will light itself.

hollow_guard.title: HOLLOW GUARD
lines: The Hollow Guard. Suits of armour, rusted and dented, walking the walls of Castle Dread with halberds, swords and the clank of metal on stone. There's nothing inside them. You can see straight through the visors.
They were contestants. They were cast as guards. They died inside the armour during filming, and over the years they rotted away, and the armour just kept walking without them.
They still guard the castle. They still salute the Count. They still go 'Halt! Who goes there?' in hollow, echoing voices, even though they haven't had lungs for forty years.
Strengths: they're armoured head to foot, they patrol in formation and they hit hard. Weaknesses: their joints. Hit the gaps.
Kill one and it collapses into a pile of armour with a clatter, and a tiny puff of grey dust comes out of the helmet. That's him. That's all that's left.

portcullis_knight.title: PORTCULLIS KNIGHT
portcullis_knight.sub: Boss of the Gatehouse. Lowers the drawbridge.
lines: The Portcullis Knight. A colossal suit of armour, nine feet tall, with a portcullis welded to the front of its helmet as a visor and a great chain wrapped round one arm that drops the drawbridge into Castle Dread.

He guards the gate. Nobody gets into Castle Dread without beating him, and nobody has, this season. He's been standing at the gate for forty years, and the drawbridge only drops for whoever proves themselves.
There's someone in this one, unlike the other guards. Someone very old, very tired, sealed in when the armour was forged. You can hear him breathing, slow and wet, behind the portcullis.
Strengths: he's armoured, he swings that chain like a flail and his charge shakes the gatehouse. Weaknesses: his weight. He's slow to turn.
Beat him and he'll kneel, and lower the bridge, and raise his portcullis visor. Look inside. Then wish you hadn't.

the_ossuary.title: THE OSSUARY
the_ossuary.sub: Boss of the Crypts. Conducts the Bone Choir.
lines: The Ossuary. A great creature made of skulls and bones, stacked into the shape of a conductor, with a femur for a baton and a choir of skeletons arranged before it in the vaults beneath Castle Dread.

Everyone who dies in Castle Dread ends up in the crypts eventually. The Ossuary collects the bones, cleans them and arranges them. Some it adds to itself. The rest join the Bone Choir and sing, forever, in a sound like wind through a cemetery.
The crypts connect to everything. Secret passages run from here to every tower, every dungeon and every chapel. The Ossuary knows them all. It's been conducting down here, in the dark, for decades.
Strengths: bone spears, a choir whose song damages you and the ability to pull bones from the walls to rebuild itself. Weaknesses: break the baton. No conductor, no choir.
Silence it and the crypt goes quiet, and you'll hear the castle above you, creaking, waiting for Act Five.

the_count.title: THE COUNT
the_count.sub: Floor Boss of the Keep. Never stopped playing the part.
lines: The Count. A tall, gaunt man in a black cloak lined with red silk, with slicked-back hair, a widow's peak, two very long canines and the most magnificent, theatrical, over-the-top voice you have ever heard in your life.

He's an actor. He was cast as the Count of Season Nine, the Network's horror season, and when the season ended, he didn't. He stayed in the Keep, in costume, in character, and he's been playing the Count every night for forty years, for an audience that died decades ago.
He's not a vampire. He thinks he's a vampire. He's committed so hard to the role that it's become true in every way that matters. He drinks blood. Not because he needs to. Because the Count would.
Strengths: he's fast, he summons the castle against you and his monologues drain your will to live. Weaknesses: he needs his audience. Give him a better ending.
Give the Count his final curtain. When he dies, he'll take a bow. A real, deep, perfect bow. And somewhere, far away, someone will be clapping.

cable_crawler.title: CABLE CRAWLER
cable_crawler.sub: The Cold Store's wiring. It moves.
lines: Cable Crawlers. Knotted bundles of thick black wire with sparking copper ends for heads, coiling across the frozen floors of the Cold Store like snakes made of electrical tape.

They're the Builders' wiring, gone feral. They carry power from the Core to every rack on the floor, and somewhere along the way, they started thinking for themselves. Mainly about where the warmth is. And it's in you.
They wrap round you to steal your heat. It feels like a hug. Then it feels like a tourniquet. Then it feels like a defibrillator, a very angry one.
Strengths: they shock, they strangle and they come up out of the floor. Weaknesses: cut them. They're cables.
Never step on one in the dark. They don't like it. Neither will you.

cable_mother.title: CABLE MOTHER
cable_mother.sub: Boss of the Cable Jungle. Strangling the power line.
lines: The Cable Mother. A vast tangle of cable the size of a house in the heart of the Cable Jungle, with a thousand sparking heads and a nest of cable crawlers writhing around her like spaghetti in a pot.

She's wrapped herself around the Warm Room's power line. Every bit of heat in the Cold Store passes through her, and she's taking her cut. That's why it's so bloody cold. She's keeping the warm for her children.
She doesn't know she's hurting anyone. She's a mother. She's just looking after her own.
Strengths: she shocks, she strangles and she births crawlers endlessly. Weaknesses: insulation. Cut her off from the power.
Cut her loose and the heat floods back into the Warm Room's lines. Everyone on the floor will feel it. Some of them will cry.

fan_wraith.title: FAN WRAITH
lines: Fan Wraiths. Pale, whirling ghosts that spin like the blades of a cooling fan, with faces that blur as they turn, howling in the freezing wind of the Cooling Towers.
They're the souls of contestants who froze to death on the Cold Store, sucked into the cooling system and spun round and round forever, keeping the Builders' servers at the right temperature.
They're cold. So cold. Being touched by one is like being dunked in an ice bath by someone who hates you.
Strengths: freezing gusts, blades that cut and they spin away faster than you can follow. Weaknesses: heat. Get near a fire and they scatter.
If you hear whirring in the dark, get to a fire. Now.

fan_wraith_king.title: FAN WRAITH KING
fan_wraith_king.sub: Boss of the Cooling Towers. The coldest thing in the Stack.
lines: The Fan Wraith King. A colossal whirling spirit at the top of the tallest Cooling Tower, a vortex of ice and screaming faces, spinning so fast you can hear it from across the floor.
He keeps the Builders' memory cold. Everything in the Cold Store depends on it. If the towers stop, the servers overheat, and every record the Builders ever made melts into nothing.
He is the reason everyone's freezing. And he's the reason anything survived at all.
Strengths: blizzards, wraiths and a spin that throws you off the tower. Weaknesses: stop the fan.
Beat him, and the towers slow, and for a little while, the Cold Store is just cold, instead of murderous.

bit_rot.title: BIT ROT
lines: Bit Rot. Shapeless, glitching creatures made of corrupted data: flickering blocks of colour, scrambled pixels and fragments of faces that never quite resolve, crawling across the frozen racks.
They're what happens to memory that's been stored too long. The Builders' records are rotting, and the rot has started to walk. Every byte that goes bad crawls out of the servers and joins them.
They eat good data. Including yours. Get bitten by Bit Rot and you'll forget things. Small things at first. Your shoe size. Your mum's maiden name. The way out.
Strengths: corruption that drains your abilities, they're hard to hit and there's always more rot. Weaknesses: backups. Restore what they've eaten.
If you forget something important after fighting them, don't panic. It might come back. Probably not, though.

the_backup.title: THE BACKUP
the_backup.sub: Boss of the Tape Library. A copy of everything.
lines: The Backup. A towering figure built of magnetic tape reels, spinning and whirring, with a hundred faces flickering across its surface: copies of everyone whose memory is stored in the Tape Library.

It's a backup. Of everything. Every contestant who's ever been stored here, every Builder record, every save. It contains the Builders' last message, in pieces. It also contains a version of you, from the moment you came down the stairs.
It doesn't know which version is the real one. It doesn't know if it's a copy or an original any more. It's very confused, and very, very large.
Strengths: it plays back your own attacks at you, it summons bit rot and it can restore itself. Weaknesses: overwrite it.
When it dies, the tapes unspool across the floor, and some of them are still playing, very quietly. Listen.

the_firewall.title: THE FIREWALL
the_firewall.sub: Boss of the Firewall. Access denied.
lines: The Firewall. A wall. Literally. A wall of red light and burning code, forty feet high, stretching across the Cold Store between you and the Core, with a single great eye in the middle, scanning.
Nothing gets into the Core without its permission. Not people, not data, not tapes. It checks every packet, every person, every thought, and it rejects all of them, as a matter of policy.
It's been protecting the Core from the Network for longer than the Network has existed. It doesn't know you're on the same side. It doesn't know anyone is on any side.
Strengths: it burns, it blocks, and it calls bit rot and crawlers. Weaknesses: the right credentials. Or a big enough breach.
Breach it and it flickers, and stutters, and says, in a tiny voice, 'Access granted.' It's never said that before.

the_recorder.title: THE RECORDER
the_recorder.sub: Floor Boss of the Core. Has been waiting to play this.
lines: The Recorder. An enormous reel-to-reel machine in the heart of the Core, built into the ceiling, with tapes as wide as rivers and a voice like an old wireless, crackling with age, waiting.
The Builders left it a message. Their last. It's been waiting, alone, in the cold, for someone to come and listen. It doesn't fight to kill. It fights to make you listen.

And the message is this: fans are fuel. The attention of the audience, every hour of watching, every cheer, every view, is power. The Stack runs on it. The Network sells it. And you, contestant, are the furnace.
Strengths: it plays back every sound you've ever made at you, it summons wraiths and bit rot and it knows all your moves. Weaknesses: listen. Just listen.
When it's done, it'll click off, and the tape will run out, and the Core will be very, very quiet. And you'll never hear applause the same way again.
